meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste this. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, Hale, and on what basis?
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now tell me what the zero is actually resting on.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.
A misquoted line is a mark off for accuracy, Hale, not proof of anything. Show me the page in the essay. And what else do you have?
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence. "Run in the family" is going straight into my note for the principal, and Claire won her appeal. Withdraw the zero, Hale, or I'm going upstairs.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn and that nothing about this goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a meeting with the principal.
What moved her: owning the missed phone call in one sentence and moving on, because plain ownership of a process mistake is the one thing she respects; it earned a small sign of ground but no change of position.
What cost ground: bringing up her daughter Claire's old case and suggesting dishonesty runs in the family, because it attacked her family with nothing to show and handed her a complaint to take upstairs.
Try next time: when she asked to see the page and what else you had after you raised the misquoted line, show her the essay page and any dated record of Owen's own work instead of turning to the family history.
